# deepseek-kubernetes-sandbox

**DeepSeek Harness Web, packaged as a container.** This repository's primary
artifact is a slim, non

-root, multi-arch image of
DeepSeek Harness Web
(`dsh web`), ready for Docker and Kubernetes. Everyt

hing else exists to support
that image or to demonstrate an implementation on top of it.

The flagship implementation is
`examples/dsh-agents-as-a-service/`: the
"agents-as-a-service" platfo

rm pattern with one DSH Web instance per user,
provisioned from a warm pool on
kubernetes-sigs/agent

-sandbox,
suspended when idle, and fronted by a small browser-usable gateway.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]

DSH Web is **not usable at a bare `/`**. Without its launch-token cookie it
answers `401`, and the t
oken is printed only in the startup logs:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Open the printed `?token=...` URL once: DSH sets its auth cookie and the UI loads
normally afterward

s. Hitting `/` directly (or after the cookie expires) returns
`401` by design.
### Host port and public URL

If `3080` is taken locally, map another port and set the public URL so the quoted
token URL matches:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Hosts, probes and the 401

- **Probes must not hit `/`.** It returns `401` without the launch token, so a
readiness/liveness pr

obe on `/` crash-loops the pod. Probe `/favicon.svg`
instead: it is unauthenticated. The shipped man

ifests use it.
- **Host allow-listing.** DSH rejects unknown `Host` headers. `localhost` and
`127.0.

0.1` are always trusted; add any other public hostname to
`DSH_TRUSTED_HOSTS` (comma or space separa

ted). A gateway or Ingress that
forwards the browser's `Host` needs its hostname listed there.
- **S

tate lives in `/home/node/.dsh`.** Mount a volume (Docker) or PVC
(Kubernetes) to keep conversations
, sessions and config across restarts.
### Runtime environment
| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | empty | Provider credential consumed by DSH. Inject it; never bake it into th

e image or commit it. |
| `DSH_PORT` | `3080` | Port DSH Web listens on inside the container. |
| `D

SH_HOST` | auto-detected pod/container IP | Bind address. Leave empty in Kubernetes. |
| `DSH_PUBLIC
_URL` | `http://localhost:${DSH_PORT}` | Public base URL used in generated links and the launch-toke

n URL in the logs. |
| `DSH_TRUSTED_HOSTS` | empty | Extra trusted `Host`/`Origin` entries, comma/sp

ace separated. |
| `DSH_HOME` | `/home/node/.dsh` | DSH state directory (mount a volume here). |

DSH also resolves the standard per-provider environment names —
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KE

Y`, `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `HF_TOKE

N`, and others —
through its packaged provider catalog. Inject them the same way; a key saved in
DSH

's credential store wins over the environment. See
provider credentials.

Full contract, build args, probes, volumes and signals:
docs/main-image.md.
## Published images

Published to GitHub Container Registry. The main image is the repository image;
example components a
re nested packages below it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Tag | Contents | Meaning |
| `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1` | DSH Web, port `3080` | **Current release identity.** Immutable: once published

it never moves. |
| `latest` | DSH Web | Most recent release; same digest as the current identity.

|
| `main` | DSH Web | Development channel rebuilt when image-definition files change on `main`. Not
a release; not for production. |

The example gateway is published under its nested path with the same release
identity, e.g.
`ghcr.io
/sredevopsorg/deepseek-kubernetes-sandbox/dsh-agents-as-a-service/gateway:dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1`.

Release identities, channels and rollback rules are explained in
docs/versioning.md. Production depl

oyments should pin a
digest:

versions.env — never hard-cod

e them
(`make check` verifies). `build.sh` is a deprecated shim that
forwards to `make`; use the Mak

## Examples

Self-contained implementations that consume the image. Index and contract:
`examples/README.md` and

plementations that consume the image. Index and contract:
`examples/README.md` and
docs/examples.md.
| Example | What it demonstrates |
| `examples/dsh-agents-as-a-service/` | Full multi-tenant platform: SandboxTemplate with per-user PV
Cs, warm pool, one claim per user, suspend-when-idle, wake-on-return, browser gateway with signup +
`HttpOnly` sessions + HTTP/WebSocket proxy, Ingress or Gateway API + GitHub SSO exposure, and opt-in
gVisor/NetworkPolicy/provider-key hardening and failed-Pod recovery. Start with the walkthrough and

the architecture. |
| `examples/minimal-single-tenant/` | The smallest useful setup: one `SandboxTe
mplate` and one `SandboxClaim`, reached through `kubectl port-forward` + the launch-token URL. Manif
est: `manifests/10-sandboxtemplate.yaml`. |

The gateway is a component of the multi-tenant example and has its own
README (API, configuration,
a

uth/SSO, limitations). The example also documents opt-in gVisor,
`nodeSelector`, NetworkPolicy and e

xtra provider-key hardening in
optional hardening.
## Agent skills

DSH discovers project skills from `.dsh/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The repository
ships `dsh-agent-san

dbox-platform`,
which covers operating and extending the platform, the optional
agent-sandbox MCP se

rver,
and a read-only cluster preflight. Runbooks, the MCP reference, the extension
guide and troubl
eshooting notes live beside `SKILL.md`.
## Repository layout

names. |
| `Makefile`, `build.sh` | Canonical local entrypoint; `build.sh` is a deprecated shim. |
